title: What If a Star Flew Through Our Solar System?

scenes.text: What if a star flew through our solar system? One already did.
About seventy thousand years ago, a small red dwarf and its brown dwarf partner passed by at roughly 0.8 light years.
That's about five times closer than Proxima Centauri is today. Astronomers are ninety-eight percent sure it crossed the outer comet cloud.
Comet showers would need it to reach the inner cloud. Only one simulation in ten thousand did, so the flyby likely changed little.
It was too faint to see by eye, but flares can make it thousands of times brighter, for minutes or hours.
Today it's about twenty light years away. The next predicted close visitor won't arrive for at least 240,000 years.

description:
